topic: Moser's Circle Problem: The Deceptive Pattern
target_audience: High school students or undergraduate mathematics enthusiasts

sections.title: The Hook: How many pieces?
lecture_lines: Place points on a circle, connect every pair.
animations: Draw a circle (#FFFFFF) and place 1 point (#FF0000). Fill circle with 1 region (#00FF00).
Add a 2nd point (#FF0000). Draw a chord (#FFFF00). Show 2 regions (#00FF00).
Add a 3rd point (#FF0000). Draw remaining chords (#FFFF00). Show 4 regions (#00FF00).
Add a 4th point (#FF0000). Draw remaining chords (#FFFF00). Show 8 regions (#00FF00).
Zoom out to show the collection of circles from n=1 to 4 side-by-side.

sections.title: Pattern Recognition (The Trap)
lecture_lines: Each step seems to double the last.
animations: List the sequence: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 in a central text area (#FFFFFF).
Animate the number 16 doubling to a placeholder '32?' (#FFD700, bold).
Explain the pattern: '2 to the power of (n-1)' appearing below the sequence.

sections.title: The Reality Check (n=6)
animations: Draw a circle with 6 dots (#FFFFFF) and all possible chords (#FFFF00).
Highlight intersection points (#FF0000) using circles (scale_factor 0.4). Count them.
Display the number 31 (#FF0000, large) replacing the guessed '32' (#00FF00, crossed out).

sections.title: The Combinatorial Formula
lecture_lines: Regions equal intersections plus chords plus one.
Formula: Choose four points plus two plus one.
Each intersection adds a new region.
Each chord adds a new region too.
animations: Visualize C(n,2) as new chords adding regions (#FFFF00).
Visualize C(n,4) as intersections of two chords adding an extra region (#00FF00).
Display result for n=6 using the formula: 15 + 15 + 1 = 31 (#FFD700).
Show all terms color-coded to their visual components.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Proof
animations: Flash a 'Caution' icon (#FF0000) next to the sequence.
Type 'Verify, Don't Just Guess' (#FFFF00) below the sequence.
